title: Watch Your Watts
tagline: A live page that shows where my PC's power goes and what it costs.
what: A live dashboard for my PC's power. A smart strip measures the wall, the PC reports its own parts, and the page splits the draw into graphics card, processor and everything else, with today's cost and a badge for what the machine is doing.
built: Merged the strip's wall reading with the graphics card and processor readings into one live view
Taught it to tell idle, desktop, AI, gaming and rendering apart, switching only after 90 seconds
Built the live chart, a cost tile, and daily, weekly and monthly summaries posted to Discord
Kept the page fast by showing the last saved sample instead of waiting on the strip
credit: I wrote the collector, backend and page; the strip is a TP-Link HS300

making.problem: A smart plug gives you one number for the whole PC. I wanted to know which part was using the power, and what it cost.
how: A smart strip on the wall measures the whole PC. A small program on the PC reads the graphics card and processor and sends the numbers over every 15 seconds.
The page takes those two parts out of the wall reading, and what is left is everything else: board, drives and fans.
A set of rules reads the load and names the activity. It waits 90 seconds before changing the name, so a short spike does not flip it.
Everything is kept for 90 days, so the chart, the cost and the summaries all come from the same record.
credits: Strip: TP-Link HS300, read with the python-kasa library
Processor power: LibreHardwareMonitor. Graphics card: NVIDIA's nvidia-smi
